verifications.note: "Phase 1 of the project will transport 500 MMcfd of gas from the Dawn, Ont., trading hub and several supply and storage basins" — exact match to recorded 500.00 MMcf/d, in an article naming Millennium Pipeline Co. LLC and its 182-mile pipeline by name.

resolutions.researcher_notes: OGJ (June 2006) states Phase 1 capacity as exactly 500 MMcfd, matching the recorded value. Single independent source for this exact figure — a second, later figure exists but is NOT a match: the FERC Phase I certificate (per the FR 2006-01-19 notice, already on this row's Length/Construction refs) and NiSource's 2007 10-K (also already on this row) both state the certificated Phase I capacity as 525,400 Dth/d (~525 MMcf/d equivalent), about 5% above the recorded 500. That gap is noted here for context but the OGJ figure is what actually matches the sheet, so it is the value carried forward rather than a rounding-adjacent alternate.

verifications.note: "Millennium Pipeline Co. LLC has begun construction of its 182-mile, 30-in. natural gas pipeline" ... "an 83-mile extension of the 24-in. Empire system from a point near Rochester to Corning, NY" — confirms 30-in mainline and 24-in Empire lateral by name.

FERC SEIS notice: "about 181.7 miles of 30-inch-diameter pipeline" for Millennium's Phase I facilities, and "about 80 miles of 24-inch-diameter pipeline" for Empire's Connector Project feeding Millennium — both named to the Millennium Phase I project.

NiSource 2007 10-K: "construction began on the Millennium Pipeline, a 182-mile-long, 30-inch-diameter pipeline across New York's Southern Tier and lower Hudson Valley" — third independent confirmation of the 30-in mainline diameter.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Three independent primary/near-primary sources (trade press, FERC Federal Register notice, SEC 10-K) all confirm the 30-in mainline and the 24-in Empire Connector lateral that feeds it — two of the three recorded diameters (24, 30). The third recorded figure, 14-in, could NOT be independently confirmed in this pass: checked DT Midstream's asset page, millenniumpipeline.com/about, gem.wiki's own page (which cites only a generic EIA data-hub URL, https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php, not a specific document — not usable as a ref and not cited per standing rule 1 regardless), en.wikipedia.org (redirects to TC Energy, no pipe-diameter detail), and attempted web search for the Valley Lateral / CPV Wawayanda lateral (likely candidate for a smaller-diameter segment) — WebSearch was unavailable (session search budget exhausted) and DuckDuckGo's HTML endpoint returned a bot-check page with no results. Carrying the full recorded value forward as REFS_ADDED (2 of 3 diameters strongly corroborated) rather than UNRESOLVED, since real, verified refs now exist for the row where none did before; the 14-in gap is flagged here for a follow-up pass with search access.

No source found supports the recorded StartLocation/EndLocation (Lake Erie, NY -> Mount Vernon, NY) as the pipeline that was actually built. Multiple independent sources instead describe the built Phase I pipeline running between Corning, NY (west, interconnecting with the Empire Connector lateral near Corning/Steuben County) and Ramapo, NY (east, interconnecting with Algonquin in Rockland County): NiSource's 2007 10-K ("will begin at an interconnect with Empire ... near Corning, New York ... will extend eastward to an interconnect with Algonquin at Ramapo, New York"); the FERC FR-2006-01-19 SEIS notice (Phase I facilities run MP 190.6-376.6, terminating at the Ramapo M&R Station, replacing the ORIGINAL 2002-authorized project that would have run Lake Erie-to-Mount Vernon); and Natural Gas Intelligence's Nov. 2008 article, which states explicitly that the final built project involved "the sidestepping of Mount Vernon, NY, which had opposed the projects; and the abandonment of plans to cross Lake Erie in favor of utilizing the Empire system near the Canadian border." gem.wiki's own current page text (read only, never cited) independently states "The pipeline runs from Steuben County to Buena Vista, Rockland County" -- consistent with the built-project sources above and itself inconsistent with the sheet's Lake Erie/Mount Vernon values. Searched: DT Midstream asset page, millenniumpipeline.com/about, the FR notice, the SEC 10-K, NGI, thinkprogress.org, gem.wiki. This looks like a stale holdover from the pipeline's original (2002, unbuilt, 424-mile) design rather than the as-built ~182-mile Phase I project this row's Length/Capacity/Construction/Start values already describe -- flagging as a contradiction rather than fabricating a ref for the recorded value.

No source found supports the recorded SegmentCost of $800,000,000 USD. Natural Gas Intelligence's Nov. 2008 article states: "While FERC certified the project at a cost of $654 million, Millennium has said the final cost won't be known until after the pipeline is completed and in service." gem.wiki's own (uncited) page separately gives "Cost: US$664 million" (citing only the generic EIA data-hub page, not a specific document). Both of these land close to each other (~$654-664M) but neither is a rounding-level match to the recorded $800M -- a ~20-22% gap, not a rounding discrepancy. Searched: the OGJ, SEC 10-K, FR notice, DT Midstream, millenniumpipeline.com/about, and NGI articles already opened for this row, plus gem.wiki; none states $800M for this pipeline. Flagging as a contradiction (recorded cost appears materially overstated relative to the two closely-agreeing sources found) rather than fabricating a ref for $800M.
